blocks.text: Briefing for Lauren Heath and the management team, prepared by Michael Morris with Laura Bradley and Michelle Black. Program under way since {{fact:f:E-2018-001.start}}.
What the interviews are telling us

items: Holders who know the company well credit management with steady execution, but few could explain how the parts of the business fit together
Analysts want results explained the same way every quarter, particularly margins and capital spending
Several investors hear from the company only around results and would welcome contact between quarters
No one raised concerns about governance or disclosure; the gaps are in clarity and frequency of contact
Ownership sits mainly with a small group of long-term holders, which brings stability but limits trading liquidity
Funds that own comparable companies are largely missing from the register, and they are the natural first targets for outreach
Analyst coverage is thinner than at peers of similar size, so each published note carries more weight with holders
Michelle Black's peer benchmarking shows where the company's disclosure is lighter than the peer group's
A plain statement of what the company does and where it earns its returns, written in management's own words
A small number of themes, each supported only by figures the company has already disclosed
One agreed way of describing margins and capital spending, used on every call and in every presentation
Draft is with Lauren Heath for comment now and will be revised once the remaining interviews are written up
Michael Morris: program lead and first call on anything time-sensitive
Laura Bradley: drafts, version control, and the approval log for every item
Michelle Black: register analysis, peer benchmarking, and coverage monitoring
Weekly status by email to Lauren Heath, and a working session with the full team about once a month

blocks.text: What we need from management before the next session

items: Comments on the draft narrative from Lauren Heath and her colleagues, so the revision can start as soon as the interviews close
Approval to approach the target funds once the narrative is settled
A view on whether the program should include a non-deal roadshow or a dedicated investor event
A date for the next working session, ahead of the next results call
